extracted.intended_audience: nonprofit communications staff, PR/marketing professionals at NGOs, and nonprofit founders
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for drafting, formatting, and distributing press releases specifically for nonprofit organizations, including structure (headline, lead, dateline, body, quotes, boilerplate), when to announce events, and tips for using AI and media databases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the inverted pyramid method
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure information from most important to least important so journalists can quickly grasp the key details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with the most newsworthy facts, then add necessary context, supporting details, and quotes; end with organizational information. The pyramid method is a standard format that makes it easier for journalists to quickly understand the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start with the 5Ws
rubrics_metrics.description: Open your release by answering who, what, when, where, and why of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the 5Ws to provide the essential facts early; follow with context, supporting details, and quotes to flesh out the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline: concise, informative, and engaging
rubrics_metrics.description: The headline should be eye-catching and capture what the story is about in a few words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep it short and descriptive (example: 'Annual Fundraiser Raises Over $50,000 for Children's Hospital'). The headline is the first sentence readers see and should immediately convey the story's main point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compelling lead sentence (1–2 sentences)
rubrics_metrics.description: The opening sentence/paragraph should seize attention and succinctly summarize the purpose of the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the first paragraph one or two sentences that sum up what’s going to follow (example provided in the article). The lead builds on the headline and expands key points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include a clear dateline
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the city, state, and date in a consistent format at the top of the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A correct and accurate dateline improves credibility and helps get noticed; maintain a consistent format across releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body: explain goals and newsworthiness; focus on relevant details
rubrics_metrics.description: The body should communicate the organization’s goals and explain why the news matters, staying focused on relevant information and important details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide context, supporting facts, statistics, success stories, and any necessary background that demonstrates impact and relevance to the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use fresh, relevant quotes that add value
rubrics_metrics.description: Include direct quotes from knowledgeable people that illuminate impact or dedication and add new perspective to the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose quotes that reflect the organization's impact or demonstrate staff/volunteer dedication; quotes should be fresh and relevant (not generic). The article suggests quotes need not always come from an executive director.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include visuals and original assets
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide your organization's logo, shareable infographics, photos, and other assets to make the release more attractive and ensure accurate use by media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embedding social media posts, infographics, and ready-to-share visuals increases impact. Including original assets reduces the risk of outlets using outdated materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact information and boilerplate
rubrics_metrics.description: End with an 'About Us' boilerplate and complete media contact details so reporters can follow up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include contact names, email addresses, spokesperson phone numbers, website URL, and social media handles. Pick a spokesperson who knows the nonprofit's mission and has PR experience to speak clearly and concisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to write a nonprofit press release (timing/trigger events)
rubrics_metrics.description: Announce major milestones and notable events that merit media attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples listed: new campaign or nonprofit launch; fundraising events or volunteer days; responding to current issues or upcoming events; updates to programs or services; receiving grant funding or awards; introducing new partners/donors; appointing a new executive leader; launching a book that features the nonprofit; rebranding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main goals of a nonprofit press release
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify what the press release is intended to achieve for the organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Goals include inspiring people to support the cause (volunteer, donate, share), raising awareness, building media relationships, ensuring accuracy of information/assets, enhancing visibility and credibility, contributing to media discussions or newsjacking, and pitching both digital and traditional media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell a clear, compelling news story (storytelling + data)
rubrics_metrics.description: A press release should be more than an overview; it should be a newsworthy story that combines narrative with supporting data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use storytelling backed by data to make an emotional and factual case; include statistics, surveys, or research and provide a list of sources and additional info when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make releases easy to skim
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure and format content so busy journalists can quickly scan and find core facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use bullet points, short paragraphs, clear subheads, and concise wording to optimize readability — the article highlights bullet points as improving word choice, structure, and readability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use an Online Newsroom to increase visibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Publish releases in an online newsroom to improve search visibility and recurring discoverability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An Online Newsroom can help releases appear more often in search engines; the article cites publishing in an Online Newsroom as a visibility enhancer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted distribution via quality media databases
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitch to journalists who cover your topic using a curated database rather than broad, untargeted approaches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use pre-vetted media databases to filter relevant journalists and outlets (example: journalists covering NGOs, environment). Targeting saves time and improves the chance of pickup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveats about wire services and purchased lists
rubrics_metrics.description: Be cautious about relying solely on wire services or bought contact lists for distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wire services risk burying your release among many others and may not reach the right audience; purchased lists often contain outdated or irrelevant contacts leading to bounces and wasted effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repurpose press release content for social media
rubrics_metrics.description: Adapt the release into platform-appropriate social posts to amplify reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create bite-sized summaries tailored to each platform's audience, use compelling visuals and hashtags, and always link back to the full release to drive traffic to your site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide clear key messages for drafting
rubrics_metrics.description: When creating a release (manually or with AI), articulate the core messages you want to communicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of key message categories: Mission and Impact (what you do and outcomes), Need and Importance (why services/programs matter), and Call to Action (what you want the audience to do — donate, volunteer, share).

rubrics_metrics.name: AI-assisted drafting workflow and quality checks
rubrics_metrics.description: If using AI tools, follow a multi-step process and apply editorial checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The article recommends: (1) enter basic details (type, audience, language), (2) provide key messages, (3) answer follow-up questions to flesh out the story, (4) customize and edit the draft, and (5) use AI-suggested improvements (the AI assistant referenced reviews drafts and suggests edits based on 11 key criteria) and get journalist contact recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select quotes and spokespeople strategically
rubrics_metrics.description: Pick speakers and quotations that demonstrate impact and are likely to resonate with journalists and audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose spokespeople who know the mission and have PR experience; choose quotes that reflect impact or dedication rather than generic statements. The article explicitly advises that spokespeople don't have to be board members or executive directors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include sources and additional info when relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide links to research, surveys, or further reading to support claims in the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pointing readers to a list of sources or to documented actions (e.g., 'The Charter’s ten key actions') strengthens credibility and offers journalists material for follow-ups.
